plants.name: Colchicum autumnale
plants.description: A cormous perennial that produces goblet-shaped, crocus-like flowers in autumn, long after its leaves have died back. Flowers emerge directly from the ground without foliage, which earned it the nickname 'naked ladies'. All parts of the plant are highly toxic.
plants.bloomingSeason: Early to mid autumn (September to October)
plants.location: Native to Europe in damp meadows and woodlands; widely cultivated in temperate gardens in North America and elsewhere
plants.funFact: Colchicum is the source of colchicine, a compound used in medicine to treat gout and used by plant breeders to induce chromosome doubling.

plants.name: Symphyotrichum novae-angliae
plants.description: A tall, robust perennial wildflower with clusters of daisy-like flowers with yellow centers and many narrow ray petals. It is a vital late-season nectar source for pollinators and thrives in meadows, roadsides, and prairies.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late summer to mid autumn (August to October)
plants.location: Eastern and central North America, from Quebec to Alabama and west to the Rockies; grown widely in gardens
plants.funFact: Monarch butterflies depend on New England asters for nectar to fuel their long migration to Mexico, which coincides with peak bloom in early October.

plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: A tree with fern-like leaves that erupts in massive clusters of trumpet-shaped lavender-blue flowers, often before leaves fully emerge. In spring in the Southern Hemisphere it creates spectacular purple canopies over streets and parks.
plants.bloomingSeason: Spring in the Southern Hemisphere (October to November); begins in late September
plants.location: Native to South America (Argentina, Bolivia); widely planted in South Africa (Pretoria), Australia, and New Zealand's northern regions
plants.funFact: Pretoria in South Africa is known as the 'Jacaranda City' with tens of thousands of jacaranda trees, and fallen blossoms create purple carpets on the streets each October.

plants.name: Osmanthus fragrans
plants.description: An evergreen shrub or small tree with tiny but intensely fragrant flowers that smell of apricots and ripe peaches. The blossoms appear in clusters along the stems and perfume entire gardens and streets.
plants.location: Native to Asia, from the Himalayas through China to Japan; commonly planted in China, Japan, and the southeastern United States
plants.funFact: In China, the Osmanthus blooming season is celebrated alongside the Mid-Autumn Festival, and the flowers are used to flavor teas, wine, cakes, and jams.
